model: One-sentence engine: Hut 8 originates grid power ahead of demand, then builds turnkey AI data centers and leases them for 15 years, triple-net and take-or-pay, to investment-grade or Google-backstopped tenants, financing each campus with fully amortizing, tenor-matched, non-recourse investment-grade project bonds, while a legacy bitcoin business (about 54% of American Bitcoin, ABTC) supplies today's revenue and a bitcoin treasury (per 2Q26 release, 10-Q and call). Revenue map: (1) Lease rent = delivered critical IT MW x $/kW-month x 12, with 3.0% annual escalators; rent starts only as halls are handed over. Contracted: River Bend, Louisiana, 245 MW to Fluidstack with a Google backstop, $7.0bn base term, about $454mn average annual NOI, first hall 2Q27 and the rest over 2027 (December 2025 release); Beacon Point Phase 1, Texas, 352 MW, $9.8bn, about $655mn NOI, energization 1Q27, first hall 3Q27; Beacon Point Phase 2, 352 MW, $9.8bn, about $655mn NOI, first hall 2Q28, same AA- or higher tenant (July 2026 release, June notes release). Total 949 MW, $26.6bn base-term value, more than $1.75bn average annual NOI (2Q26 release). Average base-term rent works out to about $159 per kW-month at River Bend and $155 at Beacon Point; first full-year rent in the bond decks is about $127 (River Bend 2028, $373mn) and $129 (Beacon Point Phase 1 2029, $545mn) per kW-month (our arithmetic). Management cites about 99% NOI margins because operating costs pass through (2Q26 call). Renewal options (three 5-year) lift potential value to $17.7bn at River Bend and $50.2bn at Beacon Point. (2) Compute (2Q26 $72.5mn of $74.9mn revenue): ASIC mining, mostly via consolidated ABTC (BTC mined x price), plus Highrise AI cloud and Hut 8 Canada traditional cloud. (3) Power ($1.2mn) and Digital Infrastructure colocation ($1.3mn); the King Mountain JV share ($27.0mn of colocation revenue in 2Q) sits in equity earnings. Cost structure: today, cost of revenue ($26.9mn in 2Q26), D&A ($39.7mn), G&A ($76.1mn including $51.2mn stock comp), bitcoin marks ($138.6mn loss in 2Q), interest expense ($51.2mn) against interest income on restricted bond proceeds ($27.1mn). Straight-line depreciation; data center useful lives not reviewed here. Once leases start, triple-net pass-through leaves interest and depreciation as the main costs. Capital and funding: River Bend $3.25bn 6.192% senior secured notes due 2042, amortizing from May 2028, about 95% loan-to-cost, $184mn of equity returned to Hut 8 and no further equity expected (1Q26 release); Beacon Point Phase 1 $4.25bn 6.129% notes due 2042, Baa2, amortizing from May 2030, priced 20bp inside River Bend. Both are non-recourse, issued by single-asset subsidiaries, sized at about 1.31x and 1.34x DSCR in the bond decks. Beacon Point Phase 2 is not yet financed. Parent: $233.6mn cash and 9,314 BTC (about $557mn at the 30 June mark) at 30 June; $200mn FalconX BTC-backed term loan at 7.00% due April 2027; new $1.07bn four-year secured revolver (SOFR+175bp, LC sublimit, minimum liquidity of 40% of commitments from 1Q27 until stabilization); $1.0bn ATM with about $696mn unused (no sales in 2Q). Shares 123.26mn at 31 July. Sensitivities: hall delivery dates (rent and debt service depend on them), build cost against fixed GC pricing, tenant credit and concentration (704 of 949 MW with one tenant), cost of the Phase 2 and later financings, bitcoin price (treasury, ABTC, GAAP marks), ERCOT and Entergy power rules. GPU prices matter only indirectly, through tenant appetite. Competitive position: power-first greenfield originator with an 8,660 MW pipeline (5,400 diligence, 1,880 exclusivity, 50 development, 1,330 construction); the first single-sponsor data center to issue investment-grade construction bonds; peers include Cipher, TeraWulf, IREN, Applied Digital, Galaxy and Core Scientific. What would break it: (1) a hall slip that pushes rent past debt service dates or triggers tenant remedies; (2) a cost overrun the fixed-price contracts do not cover, needing parent equity; (3) Phase 2 or the next campus financed with dilutive equity or costlier debt; (4) weakening of the single Beacon Point tenant or the Google backstop; (5) no new leases, leaving the 8.7 GW pipeline as a cost.
